scientific_facts_for_ui.fact_1: Unlike Earth, Mars lacks a strong magnetic field and a thick atmosphere, so space radiation constantly reaches its surface.
scientific_facts_for_ui.fact_2: NASA's RadLab measurements show that hydrogen-rich water absorbs space radiation with roughly twice the efficiency of Martian rocks and soil.
scientific_facts_for_ui.fact_3: Engineers use International Space Station (ISS) measurements as a reference model to design hardened shelter rooms for astronauts on Mars.
